operations.description: Page through the audit log in sequence order. Filter by event kinds (for example egress.denied or command.denied) and outcome; pass the returned nextAfterSeq to continue. Inputs appear only as digests unless a capability allow-lists a field.

Recompute the audit log hash chain up to the current head and report any edited, removed, reordered or truncated events. A clean result proves internal consistency; compare the head with an off-host copy to rule out a full rewrite.

Read the current security posture: hardening profile, network mode, every declared destination with whether it is bound, disabled or isolated and how often it was used or denied, policy findings, audit-chain integrity and audit forwarding health. Use it to answer what this installation can reach and whether its audit trail is intact.

Bring a CRM account found with crm.account.search into this workspace. The CRM is asked to let you follow it (with your CRM access); its details then arrive through the CRM feed and stay current. The receipt proves the local request only: the account is following until then, or rejected if the CRM refuses. Adopting an account already followed returns it unchanged.
Read one followed account with its activities and whether the CRM accepted each one.

List accounts this workspace follows, in your regions, newest first: their status (following until the CRM feed delivers them, adopted, or rejected) and activity counts. total counts every match in your regions; page with offset and limit. Works while the CRM is unreachable.
Read one CRM account by its CRM ID (externalId), live, with your CRM access. An empty items list means the account does not exist or you cannot see it.

ui.exception: agents resolve a CRM ID they were given; people pick from search

operations.description: Search accounts in the CRM by name, city or industry, live, with your CRM access. Results are not stored: each carries source.fetchedAt, and local says whether this workspace already follows it. source.status unavailable means the CRM did not answer; fall back to crm.account.list. Adopt a result with crm.account.adopt before logging activities.
Integration principal only: apply CRM snapshots of followed accounts and advance the watermark. A stale from watermark conflicts.

workflows.text: Find the account with crm.account.search (or a contact with crm.contact.search, then its accountId). Results come live from the CRM and are not stored. Adopt the account with crm.account.adopt unless local already says following or adopted, then log the activity against it with crm.activity.log using the time from the source. If source.status is unavailable, use crm.account.list for accounts already adopted and say the CRM could not be searched; never invent CRM IDs.

Start with the posture. For any check that is not passing, list the matching audit events (for example kinds egress.denied, command.denied or posture.checked) and verify the chain before drawing conclusions. Report destinations by ID and state; never infer that an unbound destination was reached.
Read crm.sync.status, then list rejected accounts and open activities that were not accepted. Explain each rejection; do not retry by logging the same activity again.
